newsitem.title: MEXICO: Weekly Mexican export, import feeder summary - USDA.
newsitem.headline: Weekly Mexican export, import feeder summary - USDA.

text.p: USDA said Friday that steer calves exported to the United States from Mexico were not sold in enough numbers during the week to fix a price trend.
Exports for the week were estimated at 2,000 head into Texas and New Mexico states, against 4,032 head last week and 1,241 in the same week in 1996.
"Due to adequate mositure in Mexico, most calves are being retained on grass until fall," USDA said.
"Santa Teresa will not cross cattle until August 12 and Presidio is crossing every other week, with most other ports crossing a few head once or twice a week," it added.
Imports into Mexico of slaughter cattle were estimated to have totaled 4,000 head for the week, it said.
((--Chris Aspin, Mexico City newsroom (525) 7289530. E-mail at chris.aspin@reuters.com))
